name: Breakout Trend
rationale: Breakout rules test whether new highs or lows contain enough persistence to justify entering after confirmation rather than predicting reversals.
expected_benefit: Potential upside participation with explicit exits when price loses recent support.
failure_modes: High turnover when channels are too short.

canonical_variants.name: Donchian 20/10 long/cash
canonical_variants.description: Enter after close breaks above a 20-day high and exit after close breaks below a 10-day low.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A daily Donchian 20/10 breakout rule may improve risk-adjusted return versus buy-and-hold by entering only after confirmed upside persistence.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Improve Sharpe versus buy-and-hold and retain at least 70% of benchmark CAGR after realistic costs.

canonical_variants.name: Donchian 55/20 long/cash
canonical_variants.description: Use a slower breakout entry and medium exit channel to reduce whipsaws.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A slower daily Donchian 55/20 breakout rule may reduce whipsaw losses versus a short channel while still participating in major SPY trends.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 20% relative while retaining at least 70% of benchmark CAGR.

canonical_variants.name: Breakout with volatility target
canonical_variants.description: Combine a breakout entry/exit rule with a volatility-target risk control.
canonical_variants.hypothesis_template: A breakout rule with volatility targeting may keep drawdowns below buy-and-hold while retaining better growth than a pure cash-exit rule.
canonical_variants.minimum_acceptable_performance: Reduce max drawdown by at least 25% relative and retain at least 70% of benchmark CAGR.

suggested_validation: Predefine one channel pair before running.
Run costs because breakout systems can trade repeatedly in ranges.
Use date-window sensitivity covering bullish and sideways markets.
execution_notes: The engine supports rolling-high and rolling-low conditions plus optional volatility targeting.
